disclaimer: Fictional people and story. Screenshots and video are from the real app, with sample data labeled for this persona — not a live customer account.

personas.name: Bilal Khan
personas.goal: A daily recovery routine he can keep without guilt
personas.headline: How Bilal rebuilt a quiet morning routine
personas.summary: Bilal works late warehouse shifts in Karachi. Dawn check-ins on iPhone, craving forecast on a shared iPad at lunch, journal and SOS on laptop and phone at night — never scored, never shamed, always fictional.

day.title: Wake check-in
day.text: Still half-asleep in the dark kitchen, Bilal opens Today on his iPhone and marks how the night went — no streak banner, no red shame, just a quiet tick before the bus.
day.alt: Bilal’s Today screen on iPhone at dawn

day.title: Medicine list
day.text: He scrolls the medicine list on the same phone and ticks morning meds while the kettle boils, then drops the phone in his pocket and locks the door.

day.title: Craving forecast
day.text: On warehouse break he borrows the shared iPad and opens the craving forecast — a hard window flagged for late afternoon, so he texts his sponsor a simple “watching it.”

day.title: Journal on the laptop
day.text: At home he types three honest lines on his laptop while tea cools — private, on-device, nobody scoring the words.

day.title: SOS contacts
day.text: Before bed he opens SOS on the phone and confirms his brother and sponsor are still one tap away, names readable, no scavenger hunt through contacts.

day.title: Quiet close
day.text: Laptop stays on the desk with Today closed. He missed one tick at lunch; the app does not punish him for it.

video.transcript: Bilal checks in on iPhone at dawn, ticks meds, reads a craving forecast on iPad, journals on laptop, confirms SOS contacts, and closes the day without guilt. Fictional sample data throughout.

personas.quote: I log my day. Nobody scores me.

personas.name: Priya Sharma
personas.goal: A medicine schedule she can show at clinic visits
personas.headline: How Priya keeps her father’s meds readable
personas.summary: Priya cares for her father between work calls. Phone for quick ticks, tablet for the full schedule at appointments, laptop for export before the next visit — all fictional sample data.

day.title: Morning ticks
day.text: While toast browns, Priya opens the medicine tracker on her iPhone and ticks Dad’s morning pills in the order the clinic printed — large enough to read without glasses.

day.title: Clinic preview
day.text: In the waiting room she flips to the iPad so the nurse can see the full day schedule without flipping through a paper pad full of crossed-out times.

day.title: Notes after the visit
day.text: Back home she journals what the doctor said on her laptop — dose change, next bloodwork date — while it is still fresh, still private on the device.

day.title: Evening meds
day.text: Evening ticks happen on the phone again; she stands at the counter and clears each row before dinner, no scavenger hunt through blister packs.

day.title: Tomorrow’s plan
day.text: Before her brother visits she leaves Tomorrow open on the laptop so he can glance the plan without asking Dad to “remember everything.”

video.transcript: Priya ticks meds on iPhone, shows the schedule on iPad at clinic, journals on laptop, and closes the evening on phone. Fictional.

personas.quote: His pills are in one list now.

personas.name: Hamza Ali
personas.goal: Gentle streaks and a support contact when stress spikes
personas.headline: How Hamza stays steady through exam week
personas.summary: Hamza is a student who hates streak shaming. He checks in on his phone, uses Knowledge on a shared iPad at the hostel, and keeps SOS on the laptop he studies on.

day.title: Quick check-in
day.text: Between classes Hamza opens Today on his phone — he missed yesterday during a midterm, and the screen does not turn red or lecture him about streaks.

day.title: Learn something small
day.text: On the hostel iPad he reads a short Knowledge card about sleep debt, bookmarks nothing flashy, just something he can try tonight without buying a course.

day.title: Study laptop, SOS ready
day.text: His study laptop stays open to SOS while he revises; roommate is the contact. Knowing the button exists is half the calm.

day.title: One line journal
day.text: In bed he writes one honest sentence on the phone journal — exam dread, not a performance — then locks the screen.

day.title: Close the day
day.text: He puts the phone face-down. The app does not nag him for a second check-in or a perfect week.

video.transcript: Hamza checks in on phone, reads Knowledge on iPad, keeps SOS on laptop, journals once. Fictional exam-week sample.

personas.quote: Support is one tap. No lecture.
